generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL; never duplicated.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Sample only from the parent primary-key pool; include NULL rows (nullable FK) and parent keys with no children; never invent keys outside the parent pool (FK constraint is enforced).
generic_sampling_rules.int_numeric: Uniform integers within the column range; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side; deterministic planting of listed boundary literals.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform reals within the column range; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side; deterministic planting of listed boundary literals; ties at listed ORDER ranks.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from a small pool of realistic strings; include near-variants (case changes, one-character edits) of listed equality/IN literals; allow duplicates on DISTINCT columns (20-50% duplicate share).
generic_sampling_rules.text_date: Format 'Month YYYY' (e.g. 'August 2008'); sample months and years within a plausible range; include group sizes 1, 2 and >=3 and ties at listed ORDER ranks.
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: For each nullable column, compute the NULL share from the compact database's original values for that column; plant NULLs in generated rows to match that share, with at least one NULL row per nullable column. NOT NULL/PK columns never NULL. Planted NULLs are never replaced to satisfy a rule.

targets.require: at least two distinct dates share the maximum count

supporting_evidence.FK_publication_book: publication.Book_ID references book.Book_ID; the FK constraint is enforced, so all non-NULL FK values are drawn from the book.Book_ID pool. Unmatched-join coverage is achieved via parent rows without children and NULL FK rows, not via out-of-pool keys.
supporting_evidence.null_share: The compact database shows 0% NULLs in all nullable columns; the program computes the per-column NULL share from schema.original_values and plants NULLs to match it (at least one NULL row per nullable column).

generation_specification.uncertainty: No calculated column or date-pair order rule is evidenced; Publication_Date is a single text date column with no paired end date. Price boundary literals (5,000,000) are far below observed values; boundary rows are planted deterministically per per_column_exceptions. The unmatched_join_rows target for publication.Book_ID is satisfied by parent rows without children and NULL FK rows only; out-of-pool FK values are not generated because the FK constraint is enforced. The duplicates_for_distinct target on book.Book_ID is dropped because Book_ID is a PRIMARY KEY and cannot have duplicates.

issues.evidence: The specification's generic_sampling_rules.null_rule and the interface NULL rule require that every nullable column gets at least one NULL row per instance, with NULL share following the compact database share. Execution feedback shows generated rows with NULL shares far above the compact share (observed 0%): book.Issues 19/52, book.Title 19/52, book.Writer 19/52, publication.Book_ID 18/37, publication.Price 18/37, publication.Publication_Date 18/37, publication.Publisher 18/37. In instance.py, build_random_instance sets p = 0.0 if rng.random() < 0.3 else 0.2, and _init_sampler passes this p to the samplers; ColumnSampler.sample() returns a fresh random value with probability p, and _plant_nulls additionally forces a NULL into every nullable column. The combination yields ~35-50% NULLs, not a sparse share matching the compact 0%.
issues.requested_revision: Reduce the NULL share to match the compact database share (0% observed, so keep NULLs sparse but present). Either lower p substantially for nullable columns or make _plant_nulls the only NULL source (plant exactly one NULL per nullable column and no more), and ensure the resulting share is close to the compact share. Re-run and confirm the nullable_columns feedback lines show a small NULL count (e.g. 1 per column) rather than ~50%.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions require publication.Price comparison_boundary targets {4999999, 5000000, 5000001, 5000002} and ties_for_order_limit at rank 1 for both ASC and DESC. NumberSampler._boundary() picks a random boundary and adds ±1 or ±2 steps, but the boundary set is derived from self.elements (the literal pool plus original values). The literal pool is seeded from queries via seed_literal_pool_from_queries; the Price boundary literals 5000000 etc. only enter the pool if they appear in the supplied SQLs. The specification's supporting_evidence notes 'Price boundary literals (5,000,000) are far below observed values; boundary rows are planted explicitly per per_column_exceptions', but the program has no explicit planting of these literals — it relies on the pool. If the pool lacks 5000000, no boundary rows are generated. There is no code path that injects the specification's per_column_exceptions targets into the sampler.
issues.requested_revision: Add explicit injection of the specification's per_column_exceptions boundary values (e.g. 4999999, 5000000, 5000001, 5000002 for publication.Price) into the sampler's boundary set, independent of the literal pool, and guarantee at least one row at each boundary and a tie at rank 1 for both ASC and DESC ordering. Similarly ensure the Publisher IN literals ('Wiley','wiley','Person','person','n','N') and the Book_ID comparison boundary (4999999, 5000000, 5000001) are planted.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions require publication.Publisher aggregate_boundary with COUNT(*) values [0,1,2] and duplicates_for_distinct with 20-50% duplicate share, and book.Writer/Title/Book_ID duplicates_for_distinct with 20-50% duplicate share. The program's StringSampler draws from a small pool with p=0.2/0.0 and _plant_nulls, but there is no mechanism to guarantee a group with COUNT(*)=0 (a publisher value absent from the table), COUNT(*)=1, and COUNT(*)=2, nor to enforce a 20-50% duplicate share. The construction_pairs feedback shows only 18/65 separated pairs, and construction_pairs_by_group is empty, indicating the targeted patterns are not being exercised.
issues.requested_revision: Add explicit construction of the aggregate_boundary pattern: ensure at least one Publisher value with COUNT(*)=0 (present in the literal pool but not in the table), one with COUNT(*)=1, and one with COUNT(*)=2. Add explicit duplicate-share control for DISTINCT columns (Publisher, Writer, Title, Book_ID) to land in the 20-50% range. Re-run and confirm construction_pairs_by_group reports separation for these groups.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions require publication.Publication_Date group_sizes '1, 2 and >= 3' and ties_for_order_limit at rank 1 for COUNT(*) DESC. The program uses DateSampler with template '%Y-%m-%d' by default (since the compact values are not shown to match a template), and _init_sampler draws from original values with p. There is no code that guarantees group sizes 1, 2, and >=3 for Publication_Date, nor a tie at rank 1 for COUNT(*) DESC. The specification's text_date rule says format 'Month YYYY' (e.g. 'August 2008'), but DateSampler._TEMPLATES does not include a 'Month YYYY' template, so the specified date format is not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Add a 'Month YYYY' template (e.g. '%B %Y') to DateSampler._TEMPLATES and use it for publication.Publication_Date. Add explicit construction of group sizes 1, 2, and >=3 and a tie at rank 1 for COUNT(*) DESC. Re-run and confirm the group_sizes and ties_for_order_limit patterns are separated.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions require book.Book_ID and publication.Book_ID unmatched_join_rows with parent_rows_without_children=true and child_rows_with_null_fk=true. The program's fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws FK values only from the parent pool (compact+generated), and _plant_nulls plants a NULL in nullable FK columns. However, there is no mechanism to guarantee a parent row without children: since publication.Book_ID draws from the full book pool, every book may get a child. The specification's supporting_evidence explicitly says 'shown values include 9 and 10 not present in book sample, so unmatched child rows and NULL FK must be generated', but the program's FK sampler never invents keys outside the parent pool (per generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key 'never invent keys outside the parent pool'), so unmatched child rows cannot be generated. This is a conflict between the specification's supporting_evidence and its generic_sampling_rules.
issues.requested_revision: Resolve the conflict: either (a) allow the FK sampler to occasionally draw a key outside the parent pool to create unmatched child rows (contradicting int_foreign_key), or (b) drop the unmatched child rows requirement and rely only on parent_rows_without_children (which requires ensuring at least one book has no publication). In either case, add explicit construction to guarantee parent_rows_without_children=true and child_rows_with_null_fk=true, and update the specification to be internally consistent.

issues.evidence: The specification's supporting_evidence states 'shown values include 9 and 10 not present in book sample, so unmatched child rows and NULL FK must be generated', but generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key states 'never invent keys outside the parent pool'. These are contradictory. Additionally, the specification's null_rule says 'NULL share follows the compact database share (0% observed, so keep NULLs sparse but present)', but the program's p=0.2/0.0 plus _plant_nulls produces ~50% NULLs, and the specification does not give a concrete target share or a mechanism to achieve it.
issues.requested_revision: Make the specification internally consistent: clarify whether unmatched child rows are required (and if so, relax int_foreign_key to allow a small fraction of out-of-pool keys), and specify a concrete NULL share target (e.g. exactly one NULL per nullable column, or a share matching the compact 0% with a small epsilon) and the mechanism to achieve it. Also specify the exact date format template for Publication_Date.

unresolved_checks: Whether the literal pool actually contains the Price boundary literals (5000000 etc.) and the Publisher IN literals; the execution feedback does not report pool contents per column.
Whether the compact rows are preserved in each instance (the writer copies the original DB and appends rows, but the feedback does not report compact row counts per instance).
Whether the reproducible flag holds across runs (only one run reported).
Whether the construction_pairs_by_group being empty is due to the patterns not being separated or due to a reporting gap.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports integrity.fk_violations = 2 and validity.invalid = 2 with reason 'new_integrity_failures'. The specification's supporting_evidence explicitly requires unmatched child rows (Book_ID 9, 10) and the program implements this via spec.OUT_OF_POOL_FK_FRACTION = 0.15 in fill_foreign_keys_consistently (instance.py), which draws FK values of max(pv)+randint(1,3) outside the parent pool. However, the schema declares FOREIGN KEY (Book_ID) REFERENCES book(Book_ID), and the writer (writer.py) sets 'pragma foreign_keys = OFF' only during insert, so the resulting database contains FK violations that the integrity checker flags as new failures. The specification's int_foreign_key rule says 'never invent keys outside the parent pool', which directly contradicts the OUT_OF_POOL_FK_FRACTION relaxation. The two rules are inconsistent: either the FK constraint must be honored (no out-of-pool keys) or the specification must explicitly state that FK violations are acceptable for this database. As written, the generated instances fail the integrity check.
issues.requested_revision: Resolve the contradiction between the int_foreign_key rule ('never invent keys outside the parent pool') and the unmatched_join_rows pattern (which requires child rows with FK values not in the parent pool). Either (a) remove OUT_OF_POOL_FK_FRACTION and generate only in-pool FK values (dropping the unmatched_join_rows target for publication.Book_ID), or (b) explicitly document in the specification that FK violations are permitted for this database and adjust the integrity checker's expectations accordingly. The current state produces 2/20 invalid instances, which blocks a pass.

issues.evidence: The specification's null_rule states 'Nullable columns receive exactly one planted NULL row per instance (sparse, matching the compact 0% share)'. The execution feedback shows generated-row NULL shares far above 0%: book.Issues 15/31, book.Title 11/31, book.Writer 15/31, publication.Book_ID 20/31, publication.Price 20/31, publication.Publication_Date 20/31, publication.Publisher 20/31. This is because the program appends generated rows to the compact rows (writer.py copies orig_path then inserts), and _plant_nulls (instance.py) plants one NULL per nullable column in the generated rows, but the generated row count is small (7-8 per table) while the compact rows are also present. The '0% share' claim in the specification is inconsistent with the observed compact data (the feedback shows NULLs in generated rows at high rates) and with the program's behavior. The specification's null_share evidence ('Compact database shows 0% NULLs in all nullable columns') is contradicted by the execution feedback showing substantial NULL shares. Additionally, the interface rule requires 'a NULL share following the compact database's share for that column', which the program does not implement — it plants exactly one NULL per column regardless of the compact share.
issues.requested_revision: Correct the specification's null_rule and supporting_evidence to reflect the actual compact NULL shares (or state that the compact share is 0% and the program should match it, in which case _plant_nulls should be removed or the share computed from the compact data). The program should compute the NULL share from schema.original_values for each nullable column and plant NULLs to match that share (with at least one NULL row per nullable column), rather than a fixed NULLS_PER_COLUMN = 1. The current mismatch between the stated 0% share and the observed 15-20/31 shares is a specification/program inconsistency.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include publication.Price comparison_boundary targets [4999999, 5000000, 5000001, 5000002] and publication.Book_ID comparison_boundary targets [4999999, 5000000, 5000001]. The program's spec.BOUNDARY_VALUES declares these, and NumberSampler._boundary (values.py) plants one step on each side of a listed literal with probability 0.35. However, the semantic_rules_and_formulas require Price >= 0 and Book_ID > 0, and the boundary values are all positive, so this is consistent. But the specification's uncertainty note says 'Price boundary literals (5,000,000) are far below observed values; boundary rows are planted explicitly per per_column_exceptions' — the program does plant them, but the execution feedback does not confirm that the boundary values actually appear in the generated instances (no per-value verification is reported). The construction_pairs show 16/65 separated, which is low; the boundary literals may not be reliably planted. This is a weaker concern but worth noting: the boundary planting is probabilistic (0.35) and may not guarantee the required boundary values appear in every instance.
issues.requested_revision: Make boundary-value planting deterministic (not probabilistic) for the listed comparison_boundary literals, so that each instance is guaranteed to contain rows at the boundary values and one step on each side. Currently NumberSampler.sample uses 'if self.boundaries and r.random() < 0.35' which does not guarantee presence. Add a post-sampling enforcement step (similar to _enforce_duplicate_share / _enforce_aggregate_boundary) that overwrites specific rows with the required boundary values.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include publication.Publisher aggregate_boundary targets values [0, 1, 2] for COUNT(*), and the program's _enforce_aggregate_boundary (instance.py) sets col[0]='Wiley', col[1]='Wiley' to create COUNT=1 and COUNT=2 groups, and replaces 'Pearson' with 'Person' to create a COUNT=0 group. However, the specification's AGGREGATE_BOUNDARY absent_value is 'Pearson', but the TEXT_LITERALS for Publisher are ['Wiley', 'wiley', 'Person', 'person', 'n', 'N'] — 'Pearson' is not in the literal pool, so the COUNT=0 group is created by ensuring 'Pearson' is absent from the table (which it is by default). The logic is fragile: if the sampler happens to generate 'Pearson' (it won't, since it's not in the pool), the enforcement would replace it. More importantly, the aggregate_boundary target values [0, 1, 2] are for COUNT(*), but the specification's comparison_boundary for Publisher targets IN ('Person', 'Wiley') and IN ('Wiley', 'n') — the program's TEXT_LITERALS include these, but the enforcement only guarantees 'Wiley' appears (twice) and 'Person' appears (via replacement). It does not guarantee 'n' or 'N' appear, so the IN ('Wiley', 'n') boundary may not be exercised.
issues.requested_revision: Extend _enforce_aggregate_boundary (or add a separate enforcement) to guarantee that all TEXT_LITERALS for publication.Publisher appear in the generated rows, so that both IN ('Person', 'Wiley') and IN ('Wiley', 'n') comparison boundaries are exercised. Currently only 'Wiley' and 'Person' are guaranteed; 'n' and 'N' are not.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include publication.Publication_Date group_sizes targets '1, 2 and >= 3' and ties_for_order_limit tie_at_rank [1] direction DESC tie_on COUNT(*). The program's _enforce_group_sizes (instance.py) assigns base dates to the first rows to create groups of sizes 1, 2, 3, then repeats base[0] for remaining rows to create a tie at rank 1. However, the logic is flawed: it assigns base[idx % len(base)] for each size group, so for sizes [1,2,3] it assigns base[0] to row 0 (size 1), base[1], base[2] to rows 1-2 (size 2), base[3], base[4], base[5] to rows 3-5 (size 3). Then remaining rows (idx=6, n=7) get base[0]='August 2008'. So 'August 2008' appears at row 0 and row 6 — COUNT=2, not a tie at rank 1 with another group. The tie_at_rank [1] DESC requires at least two groups with the same maximum COUNT. The current logic does not reliably create this tie: the size-3 group (base[3], base[4], base[5] = 'October 2005', 'March 2007', 'April 2007') has COUNT=1 each, and 'August 2008' has COUNT=2, so rank 1 is unique, not tied.
issues.requested_revision: Fix _enforce_group_sizes to create a genuine tie at rank 1 for COUNT(*) DESC: ensure at least two distinct Publication_Date values each have the same maximum count (e.g., two groups of size 3, or one group of size 3 and another of size 3). The current assignment produces a unique maximum, violating the ties_for_order_limit target.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include book.Book_ID duplicates_for_distinct target duplicate_share 20-50%, and the program's DUPLICATE_SHARE_COLUMNS includes ('book', 'Book_ID'). However, book.Book_ID is the PRIMARY KEY of book, and the schema declares PRIMARY KEY (Book_ID). The program's _enforce_duplicate_share (instance.py) is called after sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates, and it overwrites values in the column to create duplicates. But book.Book_ID is a PK, so duplicates would violate the PK constraint. The execution feedback shows pk_duplicates = 0, so the writer must be dropping or the enforcement is not actually creating PK duplicates (perhaps because sample_fresh_primary_keys runs before _enforce_duplicate_share and the enforcement overwrites with values that happen to be unique, or the writer's executemany fails and falls back to per-row insert which drops duplicates). Regardless, the specification's request for a 20-50% duplicate share on a PRIMARY KEY column is semantically impossible — a PK cannot have duplicates. This is a specification error: duplicates_for_distinct on book.Book_ID contradicts the PRIMARY KEY constraint.
issues.requested_revision: Remove ('book', 'Book_ID') from DUPLICATE_SHARE_COLUMNS in spec.py and from the per_column_exceptions duplicates_for_distinct target in the specification. A PRIMARY KEY column cannot have duplicate values; the DISTINCT operation on a PK always returns all rows. The atomic-operation extraction likely mis-attributed a DISTINCT pattern to Book_ID, but the specification should not request an impossible constraint.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include publication.Publication_ID null_rows target null_share 'none (NOT NULL column)', and the program's _plant_nulls (instance.py) skips columns where cm.notnull or cm.pk_pos > 0. Publication_ID is the PRIMARY KEY, so it is correctly never NULL. However, the specification's null_targets list includes 'publication.Book_ID', 'publication.Publisher', 'publication.Publication_Date', 'publication.Price', 'book.Title', 'book.Issues', 'book.Writer' — but NOT 'publication.Publication_ID' (correct) and NOT 'book.Book_ID' (correct, PK). The program's _plant_nulls plants exactly one NULL per nullable column, but the execution feedback shows NULL shares of 15/31, 11/31, etc., which is far more than one NULL per column. This is because the compact rows already contain NULLs (the feedback says 'generated rows: NULL 15 / 31' — but the compact rows are also counted). The specification's claim of '0% NULLs in all nullable columns' is contradicted by the execution feedback. This is the same issue as issue #2 but worth flagging separately: the specification's supporting_evidence about NULL shares is factually wrong relative to the actual compact data.
issues.requested_revision: Verify the actual NULL shares in the compact database (schema.original_values) and correct the specification's supporting_evidence and null_rule accordingly. If the compact database has non-zero NULL shares, the program should match them (per the interface rule 'a NULL share following the compact database's share for that column'), not plant a fixed one NULL per column.

unresolved_checks: The construction_pairs show 16/65 separated, which is low. It is unclear whether this is due to the boundary values not being reliably planted (issue #3) or due to the queries being genuinely equivalent on the generated data. Without held-out labels, this cannot be fully resolved, but the low separation rate suggests the boundary planting should be made deterministic.

The execution feedback does not report per-value verification of the boundary literals (4999999, 5000000, 5000001, 5000002 for Price; 4999999, 5000000, 5000001 for Book_ID). It is unknown whether these values actually appear in the generated instances.

The execution feedback does not report whether the TEXT_LITERALS ('Wiley', 'wiley', 'Person', 'person', 'n', 'N') all appear in the generated Publisher column. The enforcement only guarantees 'Wiley' and 'Person'.

The execution feedback does not report whether the Publication_Date groups actually have sizes 1, 2, and >=3, or whether there is a genuine tie at rank 1 for COUNT(*) DESC. The _enforce_group_sizes logic appears flawed (issue #5).
The execution feedback does not report whether the aggregate_boundary COUNT(*) values [0, 1, 2] are actually achieved for Publisher. The enforcement logic is fragile (issue #4).

issues.evidence: spec.py declares NON_NEGATIVE = {('publication','Price'): True, ('publication','Publication_ID'): True, ('book','Book_ID'): True, ('book','Issues'): True} and the specification's semantic_rules_and_formulas require Price >= 0, Issues >= 0, Publication_ID > 0, Book_ID > 0. However, NON_NEGATIVE is never imported or used anywhere in instance.py, values.py, or writer.py. NumberSampler is constructed with unsigned=False for these columns (values.py make_column_sampler: 'unsigned' in t is False for 'real'/'int'), so it draws from (-hi, hi) and can emit negative values. _plant_boundary_values also writes v - step for each boundary literal (e.g. 4999999.0 - 1.0 = 4999998.0, still positive here, but the sampler's random draws are not constrained). The semantic rule is therefore not enforced by construction.
issues.requested_revision: Enforce the non-negative semantic rules: either pass unsigned=True to NumberSampler for the columns listed in spec.NON_NEGATIVE (and clamp boundary planting to >= 0), or add a post-sampling clamp in instance.build_random_instance that replaces negative values with a non-negative draw. Add a check that generated Price/Issues/Publication_ID/Book_ID values are >= 0 (or > 0 for the PKs).

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for publication.Book_ID comparison_boundary lists values [4999999, 5000000, 5000001] with planting 'deterministic'. spec.py BOUNDARY_VALUES only contains ('publication','Price'); the comment explicitly says publication.Book_ID boundary values are 'kept for the literal pool only' and 'NOT planted as FK values'. This is a deliberate deviation from the specification. The specification's int_foreign_key rule does say 'never invent keys outside the parent pool', so the two requirements conflict; the program resolves the conflict by dropping the boundary planting, but the specification still lists it as a required per-column exception.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: reconcile the specification — either remove the publication.Book_ID comparison_boundary exception (since it conflicts with the FK constraint) or state explicitly that it is satisfied only via the literal pool. Engineer: if the designer keeps it, document the resolution in spec.py and ensure the literal pool contains those values (it does via seed_literal_pool_from_queries).

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for publication.Publisher aggregate_boundary requires groups with COUNT(*) = 0, 1 and 2. _enforce_aggregate_boundary sets col[0]='Wiley' and col[1]='Wiley' (giving Wiley count 2), and replaces any 'Pearson' with 'Person' to make Pearson count 0. But it does not guarantee a value with COUNT(*)=1: after _enforce_text_literals plants 'Wiley','wiley','Person','person','n','N' at positions 0..5, and _enforce_aggregate_boundary overwrites positions 0 and 1 with 'Wiley', the remaining literals 'Person','person','n','N' each appear once (count 1) — so count=1 is satisfied incidentally. However, _enforce_duplicate_share runs before _enforce_text_literals and may have already collapsed values; the ordering is fragile and the count=1 guarantee is not explicit. Also, the 'absent_value' 'Pearson' is not in TEXT_LITERALS, so it may never appear and the count=0 branch is a no-op.
issues.requested_revision: Make the aggregate boundary explicit: after all other enforcement, verify (or construct) at least one Publisher value with COUNT(*)=1 and one with COUNT(*)=2, and ensure the absent value is genuinely absent (or drop the count=0 requirement if it cannot be guaranteed). Add an assertion in the instance builder.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for publication.Publication_Date group_sizes requires group sizes 1, 2 and >= 3, and ties_for_order_limit requires at least two distinct dates share the maximum count. _enforce_group_sizes builds sizes [1,2,3,3] for n >= 8, but publication has only 7 rows per instance (TABLE_SIZES = {'book': 8, 'publication': 7}). The n < 8 branch builds two groups of size n//2 (3 and 4 for n=7) and then overwrites col[n-1] and col[n-2] with base[2], producing sizes 3, 2, 2 — no group of size 1, and the tie is between two groups of size 2, not the maximum. The required group sizes 1, 2, >=3 are not all present.
issues.requested_revision: Either increase publication table size to at least 9 (so sizes [1,2,3,3] fit) or rewrite the n < 8 branch to produce sizes 1, 2, and >=3 within 7 rows (e.g. 1+2+4 = 7, with the size-4 group as the unique max, or 1+2+2+2 with a tie at 2). Add a post-construction check that the group-size multiset contains 1, 2, and >=3, and that at least two dates share the maximum count.

issues.evidence: The specification's null_rule says 'compute the NULL share from the compact database's original values for that column; plant NULLs in generated rows to match that share, with at least one NULL row per nullable column.' The compact database shows 0% NULLs in all nullable columns (supporting_evidence.null_share). The program's _plant_nulls and fill_foreign_keys_consistently both do n_null = max(1, n_null) when spec.NULL_AT_LEAST_ONE, so every nullable column gets at least one NULL even though the compact share is 0. Execution feedback confirms: book.Issues 20/50 NULL, book.Title 20/50, book.Writer 20/50, publication.Book_ID 18/32, publication.Price 17/32, publication.Publication_Date 17/32, publication.Publisher 17/32. This is a large deviation from the compact share (0%) and from the specification's null_rule, though it matches the interface's 'at least one NULL row per nullable column' requirement. The interface note says a 0/n line 'may be noted for the engineer; it does not block a pass', but here the opposite problem occurs: the program over-plants NULLs relative to the compact share.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: clarify whether the interface's 'at least one NULL per nullable column' overrides the compact-share rule when the compact share is 0. If so, state it explicitly in the specification. Engineer: if the compact share is 0, plant exactly one NULL per nullable column (not ~50%), so the generated NULL share is close to the compact share while still satisfying the interface minimum. Currently the NULL share is ~50-60%, far above the compact 0%.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for publication.Price ties_for_order_limit requires tie_at_rank [1] for both ASC and DESC. _plant_boundary_values plants 4999999, 4999998, 5000000, 4999999, 5000001, 5000000, 5000002, 5000001, 5000003, 5000002, 5000004, 5000003 (cycling) — this creates ties at 4999999, 5000000, 5000001, 5000002, 5000003, but the maximum value 5000004 appears once, so there is no tie at rank 1 for DESC. For ASC, the minimum 4999998 appears once, so no tie at rank 1 for ASC either. The tie requirement is not satisfied.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure the maximum (for DESC) and minimum (for ASC) Price values each appear at least twice. E.g. plant the boundary sequence so that the largest planted value is duplicated, and the smallest is duplicated. Add a post-construction check that the max and min each have count >= 2.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for publication.Price rows_with_different_values requires '>= 2 per group with different values' for scalar SELECT(MAX(publication.price)). The program plants boundary values but does not guarantee that any group (e.g. by Publisher or Book_ID) has at least two rows with different Price values. With 7 publication rows and 6 distinct Publisher literals plus boundary planting, groups may be singletons. No code enforces this.
issues.requested_revision: Add a construction step that ensures at least one group (by the relevant grouping column) contains >= 2 rows with different Price values, or document that the pattern is satisfied by the overall table having >= 2 distinct Price values (which it does). Clarify the intended grouping in the specification.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for publication.Publication_ID aggregate_boundary requires COUNT(DISTINCT publication_id) values [0, 1, 2]. The program uses sample_fresh_primary_keys to drop PK collisions, so all Publication_IDs are distinct; COUNT(DISTINCT) will be 7 (the table size), never 0, 1, or 2. The pattern is not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify whether the aggregate_boundary on Publication_ID is meant to be exercised via a query that filters to 0/1/2 rows (e.g. WHERE Publication_ID = X), in which case the distinct PK values suffice. If the pattern requires the table itself to have 0/1/2 distinct IDs, that conflicts with the PK and table size; the designer should remove or reinterpret it.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for book.Book_ID duplicates_for_distinct requires a 20-50% duplicate share, but Book_ID is a PRIMARY KEY. spec.py correctly drops this target (comment: 'book.Book_ID is excluded: it is a PRIMARY KEY and cannot be duplicated'). This is a correct resolution, but the specification still lists it as a required exception, creating an inconsistency between spec and program.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: remove the book.Book_ID duplicates_for_distinct exception from the specification (it is impossible under the PK constraint). Engineer: no change needed; the program's resolution is correct.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for publication.Publisher comparison_boundary requires values ['Wiley','wiley','Person','person','n','N'] with 'deterministic, all literals present'. _enforce_text_literals plants them at positions 0..5, but _enforce_aggregate_boundary then overwrites positions 0 and 1 with 'Wiley', so 'wiley' and 'Person' may be lost. The order of enforcement (_enforce_duplicate_share, _enforce_text_literals, _enforce_aggregate_boundary, _enforce_group_sizes, _plant_boundary_values, _plant_nulls) means later steps can overwrite earlier planted literals. Execution feedback does not confirm all six literals are present.
issues.requested_revision: Reorder enforcement so that text literals are planted last (or re-plant after aggregate boundary), and add a post-construction assertion that all six Publisher literals appear in each instance. Similarly, ensure _plant_nulls does not overwrite planted literals (it only sets None, so it is safe, but _plant_boundary_values on Price could overwrite if Price and Publisher shared positions — they do not).

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for publication.Publication_Date date_format requires template '%B %Y' (e.g. 'August 2008'). _enforce_group_sizes uses hardcoded base dates ['August 2008','March 2008','June 2006','October 2005','March 2007','April 2007','January 2006','July 2009'] which match the template, but the DateSampler is also initialized with template=spec.DATE_TEMPLATE only when (table,column) in GROUP_SIZE_TARGETS. For other date columns (none here) the template would be inferred. This is consistent, but the hardcoded base list is not derived from spec.DATE_TEMPLATE and could drift.
issues.requested_revision: Derive the base date list from spec.DATE_TEMPLATE (e.g. format datetime objects with the template) rather than hardcoding, so the date format rule is enforced by construction for all date columns.

The instance builder's sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates should prevent this, but the skip indicates a residual inconsistency (e.g. a generated Publication_ID colliding with a compact row, or a FK value not in the parent pool after parent PK filtering).
issues.requested_revision: Investigate the skipped publication row: log which constraint failed and why. Ensure sample_fresh_primary_keys uses the compact PK set correctly (it does via taken) and that FK values are drawn from the final parent PK set (the code re-filters self-referencing FKs but not cross-table FKs after parent PK filtering). Add a post-construction validation that no row will be skipped.

issues.evidence: spec.py sets TABLE_SIZES = {'book': 8, 'publication': 10}, but the specification's table_sizes_per_instance is {'book': 8, 'publication': 7}. The comment in spec.py admits this is a deliberate deviation ('We append a few extra rows to publication so the per-column-order/likeness patterns fit'). Execution feedback shows rows_added publication: 19 over 20 instances (~1/instance) and 6 skipped, consistent with the inflated size.
issues.requested_revision: Restore publication size to 7 per the specification, or justify the deviation against the specification rather than silently overriding it. If 7 rows cannot satisfy the Price tie / group-size / duplicate-share patterns simultaneously, the specification's per_column_exceptions must be reconciled (e.g. relax tie_at_rank or duplicate share) rather than changing table sizes.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: publication rows_skipped = 6 across 20 instances, and validity reports 1 invalid instance with reason 'no_rows_added'. The writer (writer.py) silently drops rows that fail constraints and only counts them; the instance builder's PK-freshness and FK logic does not guarantee that all generated publication rows survive insertion. This means some instances do not actually contain the specified patterns (Price boundaries, Publisher literals, date group sizes) because the rows carrying them were skipped.
issues.requested_revision: Make the instance builder produce rows that all insert successfully (e.g. ensure generated PKs never collide with compact PKs after the FK/NULL passes, and that FK values remain in-pool after any filtering). At minimum, fail the unit (raise) when rows_skipped > 0 for a table that carries required patterns, so the generator does not emit instances that silently violate the specification. The 'no_rows_added' invalid instance must be eliminated.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_enforce_duplicate_share` computes `target = max(1, int(round(n * rng.uniform(lo, hi))))` and then keeps the first `n-target` values distinct and repeats earlier values for the rest. With publication n=10 and duplicate share 20-50%, target is 2-5, so 5-8 distinct values remain — but the same column also has `_enforce_text_literals_final` overwriting positions 0..5 with the six Publisher literals, and `_enforce_aggregate_boundary` overwriting positions start..start+1 with 'Wiley'. These passes run in the order duplicate_share -> aggregate_boundary -> ... -> text_literals_final, so the final literal pass can destroy the duplicate-share structure and the aggregate-boundary structure. The comment in `_enforce_aggregate_boundary` even contains a dead `if not hasattr(...): pass` block, indicating the pass was not carefully integrated.
issues.requested_revision: Order the enforcement passes so that later passes do not invalidate earlier ones, or make each pass idempotent w.r.t. the others (e.g. reserve disjoint position ranges, or re-run duplicate-share and aggregate-boundary checks after the final literal pass and assert they still hold). Add an assertion that after all passes: (a) Publisher has a value with COUNT(*)=1 and a value with COUNT(*)=2, (b) all six TEXT_LITERALS are present, (c) duplicate share is in [0.20, 0.50].

issues.evidence: instance.py `_enforce_group_sizes` builds plan [1, 2, m, m] with m = max(3, (n-3)//2). For publication n=10 (spec size 7, but program uses 10), m = 3, plan = [1,2,3,3] = 9 rows, then the remaining 1 row is assigned to dates[3], making sizes [1,2,3,4] — the max count 4 is unique, so the required tie at rank 1 for COUNT(*) DESC is NOT produced. The code then has a fallback that rewrites one row of the top date into another date, but this fallback only triggers when `sum(1 for v in cnt.values() if v == mx) < 2`; with sizes [1,2,3,4] the max is 4 (unique), so the fallback does run — but it rewrites one row of the top date into `other`, which may be dates[0] (size 1), producing [2,2,3,3] — now the max is 3 shared by two dates, which does satisfy the tie, but the size-1 group is destroyed. The net result is that the 'group sizes 1, 2 and >=3' target is not reliably satisfied together with the tie.
issues.requested_revision: Construct the date column explicitly to satisfy all four constraints simultaneously: at least one group of size 1, one of size 2, one of size >=3, and at least two distinct dates sharing the maximum count. For n=7 (spec size) a valid plan is [1,2,2,2] (sizes 1,2,2,2 — max 2 shared by three dates, but no group >=3) or [1,2,4] (no tie) — so the specification's targets are infeasible at n=7 with a single date column. The designer must reconcile: either relax the tie requirement, or increase publication size in the specification (not just in the program).

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions require publication.Publication_Date to have group sizes 1, 2 and >=3 AND a tie at rank 1 for COUNT(*) DESC, with publication size 7. As shown above, 7 rows cannot simultaneously contain a size-1 group, a size-2 group, a size->=3 group, and two dates tied at the maximum count (minimum rows needed: 1+2+3+3 = 9). The program's workaround (size 10) violates the specification's table size.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) increase publication size in the specification to at least 9 (and update table_sizes_per_instance), or (b) drop the tie_at_rank requirement for Publication_Date, or (c) drop the group-size >=3 requirement. The specification and program must agree on a feasible set of targets.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include publication.Book_ID comparison_boundary with values [4999999, 5000000, 5000001], but publication.Book_ID is a foreign key to book.Book_ID, and book.Book_ID is a primary key starting at 1. The specification's own uncertainty note acknowledges this conflict ('out-of-pool FK values are not generated because the FK constraint is enforced'). The program (spec.py) documents that these boundary values are 'NOT planted as FK values' and relies on the literal pool instead. This means the comparison_boundary pattern for publication.Book_ID is not actually implemented in the generated data.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the publication.Book_ID comparison_boundary from the specification (it is infeasible under the FK constraint), or explicitly mark it as satisfied only via the literal pool (not via generated rows). The specification should not list a per_column_exception that the program cannot implement.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows nullable columns with very high NULL shares in generated rows: book.Issues 19/47, book.Title 19/47, book.Writer 19/47, publication.Book_ID 13/23, publication.Price 11/23, publication.Publication_Date 12/23, publication.Publisher 12/23. The compact database has 0% NULLs in all nullable columns (per supporting_evidence). The program's `_plant_nulls` plants exactly one NULL per nullable column when the compact share is zero, but the execution feedback shows ~40-50% NULL shares. This is because `_init_sampler` and the samplers can return None? No — the samplers drop None. The high NULL counts must come from `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` and `_plant_nulls` being applied to columns that already have many NULLs, or from the writer skipping non-NULL rows. In any case, the generated NULL share does not follow the compact share (0%), violating the NULL rule.
issues.requested_revision: Investigate why generated NULL shares are ~40-50% when the compact share is 0%. The NULL rule requires the share to follow the compact share (0%) with at least one NULL per nullable column. The program should plant exactly one NULL per nullable column (as the comment claims) and no more. Add an assertion after generation that the NULL count per nullable column is exactly 1 (when compact share is 0).

issues.evidence: instance.py `_enforce_price_ties` uses `spec.PRICE_TIE_MIN = 2` and `spec.PRICE_TIE_MAX = 2`, and `_plant_boundary_values` plants the four Price boundary values [4999999, 5000000, 5000001, 5000002] at positions 0..11 (cycled). With publication n=10, the boundary values occupy positions 0..9 (all rows), so the min (4999999) and max (5000002) each appear at least twice — but `_enforce_price_ties` then rewrites positions to top up min_v and max_v, potentially overwriting the boundary values. The order of passes is `_plant_boundary_values` then `_enforce_price_ties`, so the tie enforcement can destroy the boundary planting. The specification requires both the boundary values AND the ties.
issues.requested_revision: Make `_enforce_price_ties` preserve the boundary values (e.g. only rewrite positions that do not hold a boundary value, or plant boundary values after tie enforcement and verify both). Add an assertion that after all passes, all four Price boundary values are present and min/max each appear >= 2 times.
